sam_runtime: quick follow-up on RFC-123 — thinking through an operational model for stream handoff + retries. want to capture tradeoffs before i update the doc.
caroline_arch: cool. what parts are still fuzzy?
dmitry_infra: main gap for me is how we surface "resumeability" to callers and how much state we keep at the gateway vs edge.
sam_runtime: exactly. options i sketched: 1) opaque resume token issued by runtime + short server-side cache (memory) 2) client-supplied idempotency + resume window 3) stateless resume using token that encodes last-ack'ed sequence and signature.
maya_sre: from SRE POV we need bounded memory per-connection. so option 1 worries me unless we size cache + evict policy strictly. also eviction means resume can fail and we need clear fallback.
caroline_arch: agree. tradeoffs: option1 simpler to implement (store small buffer + kv), but adds memory pressure. option3 avoids server cache but requires crypto + backwards-compat and larger token sizes. option2 pushes complexity to clients.
sam_runtime: also want to think about retry budgeting at the gateway level — we should prefer short fast retries (same node) vs full re-route. propose header X-RW-Retry-Budget with integer budget left, decremented by proxies during reroutes.
dmitry_infra: we already expose per-route rate limits; adding a retry-budget per-request feels ok if we treat it like a token consumed on failover. how do we initialize it? default 2?
maya_sre: default 1 is safer. remember a misbehaving client could cause retry storms. we can always tune via per-tenant policy.
caroline_arch: also need a deterministic handshake sequence when we pass a streaming connection from gateway->edge->runtime during a graceful drain. i sketched a 3-way: INIT (gateway->edge: reserve slot), SHARD/HANDOFF (edge responds with resume_token or resume_not_supported), CONFIRM (gateway begins redirecting bytes). snippet:```http
POST /handoff HTTP/1.1
Host: edge01.internal
X-Req-ID: r-123
X-Resume-Token: none or abc...
X-RW-Retry-Budget: 1
```
sam_runtime: with that, runtime can reply with `X-Resume-Token` if it has cached state. if it can't resume, it returns 412 and we abort with a graceful failure that asks the client to retry from start (or to fall back to CPU-hosted variant).
dmitry_infra: question: do we stream the buffered tokens across the handoff, or just rely on resume token? streaming the buffer is heavy on network and ordering.
caroline_arch: I prefer not to ship opaque audio/text buffers during handoff. instead, keep a small in-memory cache on target node and pass token. only if token missing do we transfer a small tail (<=64KB) as `handoff_payload` with backpressure.
maya_sre: define limits: max_resume_payload = 65536, max_cached_entries = configurable per-node, eviction = LRU + age 30s. also set metric labels for "resume_attempts", "resume_hits", "resume_misses".
sam_runtime: agreed. define semantics: resume_token valid for N seconds (default 60s) and consumes 1 retry-budget when used for cross-node reroute. same-node resume should be free and not decrement budget.
dmitry_infra: implementational note: we need idempotency for the resume operation: resume token must include stream_offset and model-state-hash so runtime can validate. format: base64(json({offset, seq, node, ts, sig})).
caroline_arch: add compatibility surface: runtime should expose capability header `X-Edge-Resume: true|false` so gateway can quickly choose fallback strategies.
maya_sre: observability: log correlation id + resume_token_hash (not token) so we don't leak PII. add SLO: resume_success_rate >= 99.5% for same-node handoffs.
sam_runtime: action items: 1) i'll update RFC-123 with the handshake sequence + headers + budget semantics. 2) @dmitry to prototype token format and small in-memory cache API. 3) @maya to draft SRE limits and metric names. 4) @caroline to add the compatibility header and state machine diagrams.
dmitry_infra: I'll prototype this week. leaning toward `edgetoken-v1` format described above.
caroline_arch: tiny nit — we should also include `X-Resume-Window` in response when runtime supports partial transfer so gateway knows how much to buffer.
maya_sre: :thumbsup: if we pick conservative defaults we can relax later.
sam_runtime: sounds good. i'm updating RFC now. will push a small strawman proto for review. infra-bot: deploy-bot note: new branch created rfc/123-resume-handoff by sam_runtime.
